text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT — region=us-west-2, cluster=prod-gpu-01. Observed sustained GPU request queue growth for the ml-inference service; queue depth > 250 for 5m. HPA not increasing replicas (stuck at 6). Possible metrics pipeline delay. Pager routed to oncall.

jordan (oncall): ack, I'm on. paging SRE. attaching top-level numbers: token rate + client concurrency spiked ~2x at 14:11 UTC.

anya (sre): looking. first suspicion: custom metrics feed from prometheus-adapter delayed. can someone grab adapter and metrics-server logs? @miguel can you check monitoring side?

miguel (infra): mvn. checking prometheus-adapter: lots of 5xx/timeout responses to the metrics API over the last 4m. stack shows `Get /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1`: 504 gateway timeouts. metrics-server seems up.

miguel (infra): paste:
```
kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter --tail=200 | grep -E "504|timeout|error"
# results: repeated 504s to aggregator (prometheus) and scrape timeouts
kubectl -n prod get hpa ml-inference -o yaml
# status.currentReplicas: 6
# spec.maxReplicas: 24
```

anya (sre): ok HPA config is fine (max 24). HPA hasn't reacted because custom.metrics endpoint is lagging (adapter not returning metrics); HPA fallback to cpu/memory isn't enough for this workload. So scaling stalled.

jordan (oncall): customer impact? tgts: a handful of high-SLA customers seeing throttled requests and elevated latencies, some 429s returned by our fronting queue. Not yet full outage but degradation. Notifying support.

customer-support: flagged top 5 customers in the last 10m — CS will prepare a short note. ETA for customer update 30m.

anya (sre): mitigation plan (short term): 1) force HPA to scale with `kubectl patch` to bump replicas to absorb queue while we fix metrics. 2) restart prometheus-adapter pods to recover scrape path. 3) scale nodepool if cluster runs out of allocatable GPUs. I'm going to execute 1 & 2 now.

jordan (oncall): do it. also enable model-fallback routing (route heavy requests to smaller model pool) if we can quickly flip a feature flag.

miguel (infra): rolling restart adapter now:
```
kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/prometheus-adapter
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prometheus-adapter
```

miguel (infra): adapter pods coming back, but initial logs show backlog purge, some queries taking >10s. I also see ASG at 90% capacity for gpu-pool-a. If we force more replicas we may hit node limits.

anya (sre): patching HPA to set replicas=14 (temporary emergency).

anya (sre): command:
```
kubectl -n prod patch hpa ml-inference --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":14}}'
```

ops-bot: autoscaler note: current nodegroup gpu-pool-a desired=12 max=12. Cannot add nodes until ASG max increased.

miguel (infra): increasing ASG max for gpu-pool-a now (spot/ondemand mix). running provider command to set max=16.

miguel (infra): provider API accepted, new desired nodes launching. ETA ~3m for new nodes to join.

jordan (oncall): traffic shaping: switching fallback routing to smaller-model pool now to reduce per-request GPU usage. pushing flag.

jordan (oncall): applied routing tweak, reduced heavy model traffic by ~40%.

anya (sre): prometheus-adapter metrics now showing healthy scrape times, custom.metrics API returning metrics again. HPA observed metrics and is moving replicas down/up accordingly. queue depth trending down from 250 -> 80 in last 6m.

miguel (infra): new nodes joined, kube-scheduler placing pods. GPU allocatable increased. HPA can scale up to spec.maxReplicas if needed.

customer-support: sent interim status to affected customers: "We are actively mitigating increased latency due to autoscaling delays; engineering is applying mitigations and we expect recovery within 30m." Keep me posted for an update.

anya (sre): current status: incident declared P1. immediate mitigations applied: restarted prometheus-adapter, bumped HPA minReplicas temporarily, increased ASG max and launched nodes, enabled fallback routing. Impact: degraded latency and some throttles for a subset of customers; no widespread data loss.

jordan (oncall): handing off to night oncall @sam. Sam — summary: metrics adapter lag caused HPA to not see custom metrics -> no scaling -> queue growth -> GPU pool exhausted. We applied hotfixes (adapter restart, HPA min bump, nodegroup scale, routing fallback). Please monitor queue depth, adapter errors, and customer tickets. I'll join the postmortem.

sam (oncall-night): ack, taking over. will monitor for 1h and escalate if regressions. please add runbook pointer to thread and create incident ticket if not already.

ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-1142. Postmortem owner requested.

anya (sre): follow-ups: 1) add adapter liveness/readiness check tuning, 2) add fallback path when custom.metrics fails (degrade to cpu-based autoscaling or queue-based controller), 3) increase ASG cushion in us-west-2 for gpu-pool, 4) postmortem + alert tuning to reduce false negatives. Assigning owners.

jordan (oncall): thanks team. Sam, anything else before I go offline?

sam (oncall-night): all good. I have console links and will ping on-call if things bounce back. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident status: P1 -> Mitigated -> Monitoring. Last update at 14:32 UTC. Postmortem in INC-2026-1142.
